title: The mean analytic rank of quadratic twists of elliptic curves
main_claim: For every elliptic curve E/Q, the average analytic rank of E^(d) over signed squarefree d with |d|<=Y tends to 1/2 (Thm 1.1). It is deduced from the companion's density-1/2 theorem for ranks 0 and 1, plus a new unconditional tail bound (Thm 1.2). For each large R, the limsup of (1/Y) times the sum of a(E^(d)) over d with a(E^(d))>R is at most C_E/R. This comes from the count #{d in A(X): a>k} << X/k^2, valid uniformly for k up to (log X)^{3/5}, together with a Jensen bound a = O(log X).

issues.location: introduction.tex eq. (density-input); tail.tex proof of Thm 1.1; algebraic.tex
issues.description: Not a gap, a dependency. Moving from the tail bound to the exact mean 1/2 depends entirely on the companion preprint's analytic density theorem (OpenAIAnalyticDensityV2, Thm 1.2), which has no Lean formalization. The algebraic-moment corollary also uses its rank-equality claim. Within this paper, only Theorem 1.2 (the tail) is proved independently. The sibling board marks the companion as only partially audited (its graph and Heegner sections were not fully verified).
issues.evidence: 'For the analytic mean theorem, (density-input) is the only input from the companion manuscript identified in the bibliography.'

coverage:
I read every section in full: introduction, setup, analytic, weights, model, tail and algebraic. Checks I did by hand:
- Completed-derivative identity (Lemma weights:vanishing): the Mellin computation, the contour orientation and the sign factor (1+eps(-1)^k).
- Partition supports and lengths (X^{1-delta_j/4}); fixed-order weight bounds, including the majorant (1+q)_+^m <= e^{mq}; terminal mean square and the uniform absorption into 2^{-3Jk/2}.
- Gauss-sum prime-power formulas and the two-variable Euler factorization, local factor by local factor.
- Poisson lemma normalization: tau_h(l)/l over sqrt(n1 n2) equals eps*B/(sqrt(r) n1 n2). The localized error sqrt(N1N2) r^{C'}/X and the total X^{-Delta}R0^{4+2C'} <= exp(-3Delta*l/4) with eta=1/2072.
- Logarithmic second-moment induction: the inflation identity m=dp^2 and injectivity, the a=0 versus a>=1 norms, the exponent bookkeeping C0..C3, A, B (recursive coefficient L^{B-31}T^{A-31}q^{-30}), the approximate functional equation (sign and orientation), the vector strip principle and the order in which constants are chosen. The base case at M=1 has no dual frequencies, as claimed.
- Model section: mollifier length R_j <= X^{eta*delta_j/4}; the 64th-moment model-to-integer transfer (needs sqrt(k0) >= 256); exceptional proportions in the good event; local shift-cost and exact-norm bounds at shifts s/2+i*theta*s and (1+i*theta)/l; relative truncation via Cauchy's coefficient estimate; the global power approximation (ratio <= e^r, maximum at z=r); the Fourier scaling y = s*log n in the first-piece error.
- Tail assembly: Chebyshev thresholds, the inequalities H_j P_j in [1/2,2] and P_j <= 2^{jk/8}P_0 give |S_0| >= a*P0/4 against a sum O(2^{-3k/8})P0; the parity step at k-1.
- Jensen bound (strip principle on L/(s+2)^4, |L(2)| >= (zeta(4)/zeta(2))^2, radii 2 and 5/2); integer-tail summation and dyadic covering; the final mean deduction; the algebraic corollary via Cauchy-Schwarz with Koymans-Smith.
I did not independently verify the companion density theorem, the Koymans-Smith Theorem 1.4 specialization, or Li's results (cited only as motivation, not as inputs).
sibling_notes: The family 006 board had one entry: the companion 'Goldfelds-analytic-density-conjecture-and-the-2-converse-for-elliptic-curves-October-7-2026', marked no_gap_found but as a partial audit (graph section 07, irreducible sections 09-10 and the Heegner local-switch internals were not fully verified). It matters because Theorem 1.1 here takes that companion's density theorem as its only external input. The tail theorem proved here does not depend on it. I posted my verdict to the board.
